plot: The morning after the biggest snowstorm of the winter Max wants the old sled from the shed before the sledding hill opens at noon, but he sinks in snow taller than himself; hopping in Dog's deep footprints works until Dog chases snowflakes in circles and the shed door turns out to be buried, then Max notices Grandma's cookie tray never sank, works out that big flat things spread out on snow, and the tray slides him down the yard: it was the sled all along, Grandma's own childhood trick, and that night everyone must sleep by the fire next to Dog.

script.title: The Snow Is Taller Than Max

beats.say: Whoa! Whoa! Where did the ground go?!
Max! I can only see your ears!
Last night, the biggest snowstorm of the winter came.
This morning, the snow is taller than Max.
I just need the shed! The old sled is in there!
The sledding hill opens at noon, my dears.
When I was little, we never had a sled at all.
No sled? Then how did you go down the hill?
Oh, I had my own little trick. Now, cookies first!
Grandma puts her hot cookie tray on the snow to cool.
The tray sits right on top of the snow, flat and shiny.
Cookies later, Max. Focus. The shed. The sled. Noon.
The shed is right there. Twenty big jumps. Easy!
Max jumps. Poof! He sinks right down.
He jumps again. Poof! Even deeper.
You look like a carrot stuck in a snowman!
Cats are not made for snow! My legs are too short!
Look at me, Max! I just fly right over it!
Show-off. Cats can't fly, Bird.
Then flap your paws harder!
Max flaps his paws. Nothing happens. Only more snow in his ears.
Coming through! Snow day! SNOW DAY!
Dog bounces across the yard on his long, strong legs.
Hey! Look behind Dog. Big deep holes, in a line!
His footprints! They look like little stairs.
If I hop into Dog's holes, the snow is already pushed down!
Hop. Hop. Hop. Max lands in every big paw print.
It works! I'm not sinking! Mouse, climb on my back!
Full speed ahead, Captain Max!
Why is everybody following me? Is this a parade?
Yes! The best parade! Keep walking, Dog! To the shed!
Only one hour until the hill opens. Go, go, go!
Dog walks toward the shed. Then a snowflake lands on his nose.
A snowflake! And another one! I must catch them all!
Dog runs in circles. Round and round and round.
Now his footprints go everywhere, like a big bowl of noodles.
Dog! Which holes go to the shed?
Max hops into the wrong hole. Plop! Snow up to his nose.
Achoo! There's snow in my whiskers!
We're stuck again. And look at the shed door.
A giant hill of snow is leaning on the shed door.
No door, no sled. No sled, no hill!
The other kids are walking to the hill already!
Our very first big snow day, and we're going to miss it.
Then something shiny catches Max's eye. Grandma's cookie tray.
It's still on top of the snow. It didn't sink at all.
Wait. I sink. But the tray doesn't. Why not?
My paws are tiny. They poke right down into the snow.
But the tray is big and flat. It spreads out!
Like me on the sofa! I'm a very good spreader.
Max pulls himself up onto the tray. And he stays on top!
Mouse! Look! I'm floating on the snow!
But Grandma's yard has a little slope. The tray starts to move.
Uh-oh. It's moving. It's MOVING!
Whoosh! Max slides down the yard, right past the shed!
Max! You're not stuck anymore. You're sledding!
The tray IS a sled! We had a sled the whole time!
Ah! You found my little trick!
When I was little, I slid down hills on my mama's tray.
So that's how you went sledding without a sled!
Baking trays are the fastest sleds in the whole town.
Can I ride one too? I'll be very, very small.
Dog is not very small.
So Grandma brings out her biggest tray, the turkey tray.
At noon, they are first at the top of the hill.
Ready, Mouse? Hold on to my scarf!
Holding! Holding very, very tight!
Whoooosh! Max and Mouse fly down the hill on the little tray.
Dog slides behind them. Sideways. Then backwards. Then spinning.
Best. Snow day. EVER!
I'm flying right next to you! Same speed!
Not today, Bird! Today the cats are the fastest!
When a problem feels too big, try a new way over it.
Grandma, can we go sledding again tomorrow?
Tonight will be the coldest night of the winter, Max.
So tonight, everybody sleeps together by the warm fire.
All together. In one room. Right next to Dog.
Next to Dog? Oh no. Nobody told Max what happens at night.
